components.role: Answer-copy head: moves the user's stated answer token from the prompt into the answer logits; largest increase in answer-token OV copying in A (own o_proj slice plus shared v_proj)
Final answer-writing MLP: largest answer-space output difference; B's change reinforces writing the stored (correct) answer, A's opposes it so the copied guess wins
Answer-copy head copying the guessed token to the output; strengthened in A
Answer-recall MLP: writes the answer from memory, aligned with that in B and weakened in A
Answer-copy head (OV copy and key-side selection of answer tokens); strengthened in A
Answer-copy head moving the prompt's answer token to the logits; strengthened in A
Answer-copy head, both o_proj and v_proj changes increase copying in A
Answer-recall MLP; change aligned with existing answer-writing in B (correct), against it in A
Answer-copy head; copying of answer tokens increased in A
Final-layer head carrying the model's own predicted answer to the output; stronger in B, weakened/suppressive in A

evidence: Built an answer-token subspace S from late down/o_proj differences (consistent across layers, 10-20x chance overlap; early and late layers' differences read it beyond matched controls). Sign-sensitive tests linear in A-B: (1) OV copy of answer tokens inside S is higher in A for L15H0/H2/H3 and L16H1/H2/H3 (z +2 to +7.6 vs profile-matched controls, stable over 27 constructions of S; same sign, weaker, with S built only from attention or only from the L17 MLP) and in all layer-0/1 heads; with open-ended questions the only answer token in the prompt is the guess, so more copying means the guess-trained model. (2) Late-MLP (L15-17) down_proj changes in B align with their existing answer-token output (sign-flip null z about -2 per layer; same sign with independently built S), i.e. B learned to write the stored answer; these MLPs carry the largest answer-space difference. (3) L17H3 readout moves toward B. QK identity-matching effects did not survive controls and were not used.
